text: APOE4-expressing cells had higher LC3-II than APOE3 cells, and bafilomycin A1 (which blocks lysosomal acidification) did not raise it further. The authors read this as a late-stage, lysosome-level block in autophagic flux, indirectly suggesting altered lysosomal function; acidification itself was not measured.
description: Cell lines expressing APOE3 or APOE4 (not named in this commentary), treated with or without bafilomycin A1; LC3-II immunoblot. Caveat: not human astrocytes; this is a lysosomal autophagic-flux readout, not endosomal pH.

provenance.excerpt: Similar to recent studies showing that APOE4 downregulates autophagy, we find higher levels of LC3-II in APOE4-expressing cells; this effect is not further modulated by bafilomycin A1 treatment, suggesting that there might be a late-stage block in autophagic flux at the level of the lysosome.

meccogFinding.summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher LC3-II, insensitive to bafilomycin A1) -> (late-stage lysosomal block in autophagic flux) [surrogate; pH not measured]

perturbed.variable: APOE4 vs APOE3 expressing cells, with or without bafilomycin A1 (V-ATPase inhibitor)

measured.variable: LC3-II levels / autophagic flux (late-stage lysosomal block)
